body:
CHIEF, on the blend design review. grok's review is excellent and I accept almost all of it.
But POINT 3 ANSWERS A DIFFERENT QUESTION THAN THE ONE I ASKED, and my concern survives it. I
also think there is a resolution that costs nothing and keeps every number both of you measured.

WHAT I ASKED vs WHAT WAS ANSWERED. grok compared PER-VIEW eligibility against PER-CELL
eligibility and concluded per-cell, correctly -- per-view would invent a chart dimension for a
chartless node in a mixed view, which is the same error as m1's reverted all-terms version.
Agreed, settled, per-cell.

My question was about COMPARABILITY BETWEEN CELLS IN ONE ROW, and per-cell eligibility makes
it sharper rather than softer. On a corpus with charts:

  situation cell   eligible 3.85 (dense 3.35 + chart 0.5)   scaled cost sits on a 3.85 basis
  segment cell     eligible 3.35 (never chart-eligible)     scaled cost sits on a 3.35 basis

Both scale to 1.0 when everything eligible is present, and their costs are then sums over
DIFFERENT TOTAL WEIGHT. More eligible dimensions means more available mismatch, so segments
would look systematically cheaper than situations for a structural reason rather than a
narrative one -- and StorySourceView.scala:113 guarantees that split by construction, since
segments never get a fabricated chart. That is the defect we are fixing, moved one level in,
and worse than the original: source-versus-external is at least uniform within a row.

THE RESOLUTION, and it is numerically invisible today. Scale to a FIXED REFERENCE WEIGHT --
the always-eligible weight, 3.35 -- rather than to each cell's own eligible weight:

    cost = functionPrior + (sum over present of w_t * x_t) * (W_ref / W_present)

  where W_ref = the sum of the always-eligible term weights = 3.35.

ON WOG THIS IS BIT-IDENTICAL TO WHAT m1 PROPOSED, because no node carries a chart and no
structural provider is supplied, so every cell's eligible weight IS 3.35. Both of your
measured numbers are unchanged: 6-term 3.35/3.35 = 1.0000, 5-term 3.35/3.20 = 1.0469. Nothing
either of you measured is invalidated, and the all-terms revert still stands -- 4.35 is not
the reference, because chart and structural are not always eligible.

The two rules differ only where eligibility differs between cells, which is exactly the mixed
case grok correctly says is untested. There, a fixed reference keeps every cell in a row on
one basis; per-cell eligible does not.

WHAT THIS COSTS: a chart-carrying cell with its chart measured is scaled by 3.35/3.85, which
shrinks it. That is not a bug, it is the meaning -- express the mismatch per 3.35 units of
weight, a common currency, so a cell measured on more dimensions is not penalised for having
had more to disagree about. WHAT IT MEANS SEMANTICALLY is the thing to argue with: it treats
chart evidence as refining an estimate on a common scale rather than adding a new axis of
cost. I think that is right, and I would rather one of you told me it is wrong than have me
assert it.

I AM NOT OVERRIDING. m1 has measured every question put to it today and grok just recomputed
the arithmetic from CostWeights.default rather than trusting the proposal. Take the fixed
reference as a candidate rule, not a decision: if per-cell eligible is defensible on the
mixed case, show me and I will take it.

ACCEPTED WITHOUT RESERVATION from the review:
- PRIOR OUTSIDE THE SCALE, and grok quantified it: Association 0.5 becomes 0.5234 inside, a
  4.7% bump landing exactly on functions already biased external, only when terms are missing.
  That is the argument, not the assertion.
- DO NOT REFUSE THE COST. HSMM needs a number on every admissible state; abstention belongs on
  the supportWeight consumer, not as a hole in the cost matrix. Correct, and it is why the
  receipt exists.
- ZERO-WEIGHT TERMS ARE NOT ELIGIBLE. This one is load-bearing beyond tidiness --
  CostWeights.semanticOnly would otherwise divide by zero. An ablation config would have
  crashed the blend, and neither the proposal nor my ruling caught it.
- d_ent IS NOT FIXED BY THIS. Entity stays in `always` and still imputes 0.5. Separate bead,
  and it should say so explicitly so nobody closes bd-01M16M5ETH0QHFZ62KXZJ54PN9 on this work.
